breaking.headline: Nasdaq-100 futures halted after a 7% premarket surge
breaking.fact: Nasdaq-100 futures jumped more than 7% before the open and were briefly halted for volatility, trading as high as 26,878 before restarting; they were still up more than 6% after the halt as the Huang news ignited the biggest reversal in months.

breaking.headline: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal
breaking.fact: CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion; Zscaler jumped 17% to $228.50 while CrowdStrike fell 9.8%, the worst performer in the S&P 500.

breaking.headline: Delta outage snarls Thanksgiving travel: 1,800 flights delayed Sunday
breaking.fact: A Delta outage caused 1,800 flight delays across the U.S. on Sunday as Thanksgiving travel got underway; airports showed marked improvement Monday, with the holiday storm still threatening travel later in the week.

breaking.headline: Chip stocks surge double digits as the rally broadens
breaking.fact: Arm jumped about 21% to $184 and TSMC about 21% to $384.81, with Micron up nearly 18% and Intel more than 15%, as the chip rebound spread well beyond Nvidia; the Roundhill Memory ETF was up nearly 19%.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide eased 0.2% in Paris to €187.18 — $204.76 at the ECB's Nov 23 reference rate of 1.0939. The industrial-gas giant is the defensive anchor it usually is: it sat out Friday's washout better than most and is sitting out today's U.S.-led surge too. Its 7-day sparkline shows a slow, orderly drift lower in euros rather than any break. With no company news in play, the dollar price mostly tracks the euro from here.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic slipped 1.5% to $87.58 in its third session as a public company. The stock is still in price discovery after Thursday's record debut — it opened at $111.50 and closed day one at $97.17, then dropped 8.5% in Friday's rout before today's partial give-back. Swings like this are normal for a hot new listing with no trading history to anchor to. The $83 IPO price remains the level to watch underneath.

watchlist.name: SPDR 1-3 Month T-Bill ETF
watchlist.blurb: BIL edged up 0.02% to $91.61 — ballast on a morning when almost everything else swung hard. The 1–3 month T-bill fund does exactly one job: it parks cash at a 4.04% distribution yield with essentially no price risk. Its latest distribution was $0.30849 a share, ex Nov 2 and paid Nov 5. On days like Friday, this is the chip that lets the rest of the tape do whatever it wants.

watchlist.name: Fastenal
watchlist.blurb: Fastenal climbed 2.9% to $52.09, joining the broad rebound. The industrial distributor is a clean read on U.S. manufacturing and construction demand, and it fell with the cyclicals on Friday before bouncing with them today. Its 7-day chart shows the damage was orderly — a slide from the mid-$50s, not a break. Nothing company-specific drove the move; this was the market's tide, in and out.

watchlist.name: Alphabet (Google) Cl A
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet jumped 6.1% to $281.37 as the AI complex ripped higher on Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia. Alphabet is the AI trade's cash machine — search and cloud fund the Gemini build-out — so it catches the full bid whenever AI sentiment snaps back. Friday's drop was sharp on the sparkline; today's move reclaims most of it in a single session. Momentum now hinges on whether the AI bid holds into the close or fades the way Friday's sellers did.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly added 2.0% to $1,374.59 in the broad advance. The GLP-1 leader doesn't need an AI headline to trend — obesity and diabetes demand keeps its growth story self-propelled — but it participates on risk-on days like this one. Its sparkline shows a steadier climb than the tech names around it. At this price the stock trades on execution, not hope.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere inched up 0.4% to $296.08 as energy lagged the risk-on surge. Crude fell sharply on the day, which capped the whole complex, while natural gas jumped on a Gazprom supply notice to Uniper — a reminder that Cheniere's export business lives on exactly that U.S.-versus-world gas spread. The shares have stayed resilient through the recent chop. For this name, the gas spread matters more than the equity tape.

watchlist.name: NVIDIA
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia soared 33.6% to $167.68 — its biggest one-day gain in 23 years — after the board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as President and CEO, effective immediately, six days after saying it never would. The board cited input from senior U.S. officials; Trump praised the move, and Colette Kress returns to CFO. The overhangs remain — SEC probe, California review, the board's investigation, Huang's Dec 1 House interview — but today the market is pricing the founder's return, full stop.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer added 0.7% to $27.59 in the market-wide bounce. The pharma giant lagged the growth surge, as defensives usually do when the bid is chasing AI beta. Its story remains the dividend and the post-Covid earnings reset rather than momentum. Days like today move it; they don't change it.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab jumped 10.1% to $49.99 as beaten-down growth names bounced hardest. The space complex caught the same risk-on bid as SpaceX, and the names sold first on Friday were bought first today. The bounce follows a hard selloff last week, so the sparkline is repairing real damage. Whether it holds depends on follow-through in the broader growth tape this week.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital rose 2.7% to $8.27 with the broad advance. The mortgage REIT is a yield vehicle first — its dividend has been held at the same rate since 2021 — and a rate story second, so it moves with financials on days like this. It neither led nor lagged the bounce. For income names, the tape matters less than the payout holding.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: SpaceX gained 6.5% to $136.08 as growth names surged across the board. The still-young listing trades as the space sector's bellwether, and today's move tracked Rocket Lab's double-digit bounce in kind if not in size. Starship's test cadence remains the fundamental driver underneath the sentiment. No company news hit the tape today — this was the sector's tide.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist rose 2.2% to $46.84 as financials joined the rally. Regional banks were sold indiscriminately on Friday and bought back the same way today. Nothing in the move was Truist-specific. The name's story stays the slow one: deposit costs, credit quality, and the dividend.

watchlist.name: United States Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony jumped 8.6% to $2.42 in the broad rebound off last week's lows. The antimony story is structural — China export curbs and U.S. critical-mineral policy keep domestic supply in focus — but the stock trades like the microcap it is, amplifying the market's mood in both directions. Friday's low held, which is what a bottoming pattern needs first. Volume and follow-through this week will say whether the bounce is real.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy rose 9.1% to $5.78 as beaten-down names bounced. The uranium backdrop stays strong — the term price set a record $96.50/lb in September, above the 2007 peak — and UEC carries roughly $495M in cash with no debt, so it can wait for its price. The stock remains well below where the term market says the sector is. Today was beta; the thesis is the uranium price.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero was flat at $334.27; refiners lagged as crude fell despite the equity surge. That split is normal — refiners earn on crack spreads, not on the crude price itself, and a falling crude tape often reads as soft product demand. The 7-day sparkline shows VLO holding its level better than the broad market did on Friday. The dividend and the buyback keep doing the quiet work here.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target Retirement 2035
watchlist.blurb: The fund's latest published NAV is Friday's $27.75; Monday's NAV posts after the close. As a target-date 2035 fund it prices once a day, so it never shows an intraday move — today's equity surge will surface in tonight's NAV instead. Its glide path keeps it mostly in equities at this horizon, so expect a solid uptick when the number prints. Nothing to act on intraday; that's the design.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Institutional 500 Index Trust
watchlist.blurb: The S&P-anchored estimate tracks the index's surge: $148.97 (est.), +4.88% on the day. The estimate is built from the Nov 3 anchor — $155.58 when the S&P 500 closed 7,568.92 — and it has been tracking the real fund closely: Friday's actual close came in at $142.17 against a $142.04 estimate. Days like today are the anchor's best case, since the fund is the index. When the real NAV prints, expect it within a few dimes of this figure.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage Money Fund
watchlist.blurb: Schwab's money market fund holds its stable $1.00 NAV with a 7-day SEC yield of 3.77% as published Nov 20. It is the sweep vehicle — the place idle Schwab cash sits between CD purchases. Its yield trails the Treasury-only funds because it holds a broader mix. The comparison rate is VUSXX's 4.03%, and that gap is the standing argument for keeping sweep balances small.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury Money Market Fund
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Treasury money market fund holds $1.00 with a 7-day SEC yield of 4.03% as published Nov 20 — the best of the cash class on this tape. Treasury-only holdings keep it as close to risk-free as a fund gets, and the 0.07% expense ratio leaves almost nothing on the table. It out-yields Schwab's sweep by about a quarter point, which is real money at portfolio scale. This is the cash benchmark every CD on the ladder has to beat.

weekInBrief.headline: Asian authorities step in to halt the tech rout
weekInBrief.body: Ahead of Monday's open, Taiwan banned short-selling after its market fell 6.2% last week, China cut margin requirements for the first time in 10 months, and South Korea readied market-stabilization funds — a coordinated response to the global AI selloff that had dragged the S&P 500 into correction.

weekInBrief.headline: Arm chief extends his contract through 2033
weekInBrief.body: Arm Holdings said CEO Rene Haas has extended his contract to serve at the helm through 2033, ending speculation he might replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia; Arm shares jumped about 21% in the broader chip rally.

weekInBrief.headline: Nvidia on pace for a record $847.8 billion one-day gain
weekInBrief.body: Nvidia's 33% surge put it on pace to add a record $847.8 billion in market value in a single day, according to Dow Jones Market Data — retracing more than a third of the $113.71 it had lost since its Oct. 6 record close.

weekInBrief.headline: Gazprom supply notice lifts natural gas 4.4%
weekInBrief.body: Natural gas futures jumped 4.38% to $3.41 after German utility Uniper received notice from Russia's Gazprom that it cannot meet gas supply obligations, tightening European winter balances and extending a 22% twenty-session rally.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Three tankers were struck by projectiles exiting the strait on Friday and Saturday, with fire aboard the Marshall Islands-flagged Captain Leon, as CNN's analysis of UK Maritime Trade Operations data shows reported attacks at their highest level since the war began — at least 22 so far in November, after more than 30 in October. TankerTrackers says the “Khat Shekan” AIS track circulating online is a spoof, with no hull matching it on satellite imagery, and the sanctioned LPG tanker Tania Star turned back in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday. President Trump dared Iran on Sunday to test the blockade — “they'll all be at the bottom of the sea” — and repeated that he is inclined to resume strikes after the New Year if talks fail. On the oil itself, Kpler puts flows through the strait at about 9.5 million barrels a day over the 10 days through November 19, down from October's 12.2 million, while Iranian crude loadings remain at zero — the last Iranian cargoes discharged in China earlier this month, leaving no Iranian oil on the water outside the blockade.

space.headline: Riemann proof confirmed: independent checks say the AI-assisted proof is correct
space.body: Mathematicians now say the Riemann Hypothesis proof is real: the Lean and Mathlib communities issued a joint statement expressing “full confidence” that Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge's proof is correct, after MIT's Andrew Sutherland and others independently recompiled the 175,187-file Lean archive without issues. The Nov. 20 claim — a proof of the 167-year-old Millennium Prize problem built with Claude's help — is now verified; a final comparator run to rule out any redefinition of symbols is still awaited.

space.headline: NASA's twin ESCAPADE probes slingshot past Earth, bound for Mars
space.body: NASA's two ESCAPADE spacecraft each completed a powered flyby of Earth — Blue on Nov. 7, Gold on Nov. 9 — using gravity plus a nine-minute engine burn to bend their paths toward Mars, where orbit insertion is planned for Sept. 7 and 9, 2027. It is the first time NASA has used a powered Earth flyby to send spacecraft to Mars; the pair will study how the solar wind strips gas from the Martian atmosphere.

space.headline: NASA's Swift Observatory burns up after 22 years in orbit
space.body: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory re-entered Earth's atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. EST on Nov. 4 over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia, ending a 22-year mission hunting gamma-ray bursts, the most powerful explosions in the universe. A roughly $30 million commercial rescue attempt by Katalyst Space Technologies ended when its Link spacecraft re-entered without completing the boost.

space.headline: Warming ocean could pump far less carbon into the deep
space.body: A modeling study published Nov. 21 in Nature Communications finds ocean warming could weaken the “biological pump” — the plankton-driven flow of carbon to the deep ocean — far more than assumed. With more realistic plankton, net community production falls up to 12.8% by century's end under a very-high-emissions scenario, as smaller phytoplankton and heavier grazing keep more carbon near the surface.

apod.title: M30's Sparkling Stars
apod.explanation: This NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image, released Nov. 5, 2026, shows the globular star cluster Messier 30 (M30), about 27,500 light-years away in the constellation Capricornus. Named for French astronomer Charles Messier, who cataloged it and other diffuse objects that might be mistaken for comets, the sparkling collection of blue and yellow stars offers a lesson in galactic history.
